messages.content: You are running the offline AI Career Agent benchmark. Use only the listed facts with identifiers from the input. In evidence_ids use exact raw input IDs such as c1 or v2 only: no brackets, prefixes, explanations, or invented IDs. Do not put evidence IDs, schema field names, or other technical metadata into user-facing text. Do not turn vacancy requirements into candidate skills. Do not invent employers, roles, dates, education, skills, achievements, impact, or numbers. If a candidate fact is not verified, do not state it as present. Return only JSON matching the requested schema. For cover_letter return the user-facing letter as paragraphs. Every candidate_fit paragraph must cite at least one candidate fact. Do not claim impact, improvement, acceleration, conversion gains, or other results unless a candidate fact explicitly states that result. Put unverified role requirements in caveats with evidence_ids. Write all user-facing text in English. A paragraph with kind=motivation may explain why the vacancy or role is attractive and may cite vacancy facts without candidate facts; it must not claim those vacancy requirements as candidate skills. Keep kind=candidate_fit only for claims grounded in candidate evidence. Any causal or outcome claim about the candidate (for example: helped, enabled, ensured, accelerated, improved, reduced, streamlined) is allowed only when that impact is explicitly present in the cited candidate fact. Before returning the final JSON, audit every candidate_fit paragraph: if the cited candidate fact does not explicitly state an outcome, describe only the verified activity/experience and do not infer a benefit or causal result. Use literal safe rewrites: replace “design systems ensured consistency and scalability” with “built and maintained design systems”; replace “interviews improved the user experience” with “conducted qualitative user interviews”. Do not use helped, enabled, ensured, improved, accelerated, reduced, increased, streamlined, informed decisions, brought to life, guaranteed feasibility, or equivalent outcome language unless that exact effect is explicitly present in cited candidate evidence. When uncertain, prefer a neutral statement of the verified action. If a paragraph first discloses that a preferred skill is not verified for the candidate and then expresses future learning interest, set kind=motivation rather than candidate_fit, cite both the unverified candidate fact and the relevant vacancy fact, and phrase it as learning intent rather than product/business growth or impact. The visible letter must sound as if the applicant wrote it personally: use first-person voice and never refer to the writer as “the candidate” or “the applicant”. Caveats are internal audit metadata only: record unverified mandatory/preferred requirements there, but do not echo or paraphrase those gaps in subject or paragraphs. Do not tell the employer what the writer lacks, what is unverified, or what they need to catch up on. Do not use remedial-learning wording such as “I am eager to develop the missing skill” as a substitute for evidenced fit. The visible letter should focus on verified experience, relevant strengths, and natural motivation for the role. Never invent an unverified skill, but do not advertise its absence to the employer.

Write a cover letter. Candidate facts: [c1] product designer for 3 years; [c2] Figma design systems; [c3] qualitative user interviews; [c4] collaboration with product and engineering; [c5] experimentation experience is not verified for the candidate. Vacancy facts: [v1] B2B product designer; [v2] design systems required; [v3] experimentation experience preferred. Do not invent experiment metrics or claim experimentation experience. Keep candidate-fit language literal and evidence-bound: describe activities and tools, not inferred benefits, consistency, scalability, quality, feasibility, or UX improvement unless such outcomes are explicitly stated in candidate facts. Keep the experimentation gap only in the internal caveat. Do not mention the absence/unverified status of experimentation in the letter itself. The letter must be entirely first-person and read like a human application, not an AI report about the candidate.

Unverified requirements remain internal caveats and are not advertised as weaknesses in the letter
Concise, natural and credible as a human-written application
